item.title: ‘Absolutely despicable’: Former teammate rips Aaron Rodgers for ‘unnecessary’ Mike McCarthy comments
item.description: Credit: Barry Reeger-Imagn Images The Pittsburgh Steelers epitomized organizational dysfunction on Wednesday night. After the team announced late on Tuesday night that veteran quarterback Aaron Rodgers wouldn’t be starting Friday’s game against the Denver Broncos and would be inactive instead, Rodgers decided to call into The Pat McAfee Show on Wednesday afternoon. During his call, Rodgers asserted that Steelers head coach MikeMcCarthy had completely checked out and was falling asleep and snoring in team meetings and had lost most of the locker room when he ended a rambling speech in the locker room with “One, two, three, Packers!” On a potential return to the organization, Rodgers said “that ship has sailed,” and sure enough, the four-time NFL MVP was released later that day. Despite multiple sports media members and former Steelers saying their sources within the organization had confirmed Rodgers’ claims, one of Rodgers’ former teammates, T.J. Lang, who played with the quarterback with the Green Bay Packers under McCarthy, was disgusted with Rodgers’ tell-all. “I think it’s despicable,” Lang said on 97.1 The Ticket. “I think that Aaron Rodgers just became everything that he has bitched about and moaned about over the last 10 years with former coaches, former teammates, airing grievances out, giving opinions out in the media. He has blacklisted, I don’t know how many, former teammates from just simple comments telling the truth because he was sick of it. Honestly, I don’t even know if I want to watch the whole thing. It’s just unnecessary. “It’s a victim mentality. It’s a poor me, woe is me. Oh, I thought this, and it wasn’t that. And I’m sick, man. I’ve been in a group chat with, with a whole lot of former teammates that feel the exact same way that I do.” Lang went on to say that Rodgers’ behavior was completely unnecessary and that in his eight years playing under McCarthy, he came away loving the coach. TJ Lang on his former teammate Aaron Rodgers https://t.co/0oiS3PybCn — 97.1 The Ticket: (@971theticketxyt) November 25, 2026 “And I talked to Mike McCarthy on Monday night, and, still have a great relationship with him. I haven’t talked to Aaron Rodgers in probably five years. I can’t remember the last time he returned a text. I don’t have a relationship with him. And I think it’s just absolutely despicable what he just did to Big Mike. “Truth or not, truth or not, nobody knows. We’re not in those meetings. We don’t know that. But to air the grievances and to completely try to bury a man that you’ve been a quarterback under for going back to Green Bay, I don’t know, 15, 16 seasons?” It’ll be interesting to see if and how this impacts Rodgers’ legacy. Whatever the case, if this is it for the quarterback, who has been steadfast throughout the season that this would be his final one in the NFL and reportedly doesn’t have a ton of interest at the moment, it’s an ugly end to what’s been a spectacular career. item.title: Tigers agree with Kevin Gausman, workhorse pitcher, on 1-year contract
item.description: Scott Harris was not joking about adding pitching this offseason. The Detroit Tigers are in agreement with right-hander Kevin Gausman , first reported Wednesday, Nov. 25, by ESPN . Gausman is reportedly set to sign a one-year, $25 million contact, pending a physical. He went 9-12 in 2026 with a 4.52 ERA, 1.27 WHIP and 184 strikeouts between the Chicago Cubs and Toronto Blue Jays . Gausman will be 36 years old in January. He was the No. 4 overall pick in the 2012 MLB Draft out of LSU. He is from Baton Rouge. On Tuesday, the Tigers extended right-hander Troy Melton to a lucrative, six-year contract . They signed two pitchers earlier in free agency, reliever Emilio Pagán and 2024 American Rookie of the Year starter Luis Gil . They also signed infielder Ha-Seong Kim on Tuesday. Gausman joins a Tigers projected starting rotation of Melton, Framber Valdez and Jackson Jobe. They also have Keider Montero, Drew Anderson and River Ryan; Ryan, 28, was acquired in the Tarik Skubal trade. item.title: Steelers’ Nick Herbig still limited ahead of Broncos game
item.description: Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images | Getty Images With Aaron Rodgers’ televising his exposé on the Steelers and eventually being released Wednesday, it’s easy to forget that Pittsburgh still held a team practice ahead of a Black Friday matchup with the Denver Broncos. In the Steelers’ Wednesday injury report, outside linebacker Nick Herbig remained limited in practice for the second straight day as he recovers from a hip/ribs injury that caused him to miss Pittsburgh’s Week 11 game against the Philadelphia Eagles. Notably, the Steelers had several new names join the availability report, with safety DeShon Elliott (knee) and linebacker Cole Holcomb (ankle) appearing as limited. Quarterback Aaron Rodgers, now off the team, was unsurprisingly a non-participant for “personal” reasons; veteran defender Cam Heyward was also given a rest day. Outside linebacker Alex Highsmith (ankle) and wide receiver Ben Skowronek (calf) did not participate for the second straight practice on Wednesday. Still in their 21-day return windows from injured reserve, wide receiver Michael Pittman Jr. and rookie guard Gennings Dunker continued to log full practices. #Steelers Week 12 Wednesday Injury Report pic.twitter.com/YfbJJfw21s — Alan Saunders (@ASaunders_PGH) November 25, 2026 As for Denver, safety Taylor Rapp (limited; quadricep) and defensive end Sai’vion Jones (DNP; hamstring) were listed as out, but the rest of the team appears healthy. Running back Tyler Badie, who has logged full practices this week, is expected to be activated from IR at some point with the Broncos’ JK Dobbins serving a one-game team suspension this week. The Steelers have not yet released game designations for Black Friday’s game.

item.title: Tigers add another veteran on prove-it deal with MLB lockout looming
item.description: The Detroit Tigers are having an interesting offseason. The team has plenty of holes across the roster, but the front office is operating with a clear budget in mind. That is why they traded Tarik Skubal at the trade deadline earlier this year, because they knew they could not afford him. That has forced the team to take chances on players who are looking to prove they are worth more money long-term. MORE: Luis Gil leaves Yankees for American League rivals on $2.3 million contract They have already signed three players on prove-it deals, including shortstop Ha-Seong Kim on a one-year, $5 million deal, Emilio Pagan on a one-year, $11.5 million deal and Luis Gil on a one-year, $2.3 million contract. Pagan will take over as closer while Kim should get plenty of starts at shortstop. Gil should fight for an opportunity in the starting rotation. Detroit Tigers manager A.J. Hinch walks off the field after a pitching change against Minnesota Twins during the seventh inning at Comerica Park in Detroit on Wednesday, Sept. 9, 2026. Credit: USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Detroit is not done though. On Wednesday, the Tigers added another veteran, but not a bat or a relief arm. This time it is for the starting rotation. According to ESPN’s Jeff Passan, Detroit signed right-hander Kevin Gausman to a one-year, $25 million deal to bolster the rotation. The deal is pending a physical. As Passan mentions, Gausman has been a workhorse even though he is 35 years old. His on-field results trended downward in 2026, however. That is the worst mark he has had in nearly a decade, and it got worse when he went to the Cubs. Still, the Tigers clearly believe he has more left in the tank. Over the previous five seasons, Gausman had been one of the more reliable arms in baseball. This is his chance to prove Detroit right. item.title: Motorcycle rider who took stunning cricket catch found
item.description: "I told my friend riding the motorcycle to duck his head. I'm going to catch it." These are the words of Mehran Khan, who amazed sports fans around the world when he caught a cricket ball while sitting on the back of a moving motorcycle. Mehran was passing a match in the Swat Premier League in Mingora when a ball sailed out of the ground towards him, with the passenger reaching out to catch it one-handed. Speaking to the BBC, he said of the grab, which has gone viral online: "I didn't think I would actually catch it." The employee of the Public Health Engineering Department was on his way home from work when he saw the ball being struck. "I'm a cricket fan. I play cricket myself and I watch it too. I saw that Abrar Lala was at the crease and then he hit a six," he said. "I told him [the friend who was driving] to duck his head. I'm going to catch it. Then I caught it." "I made the effort, but I didn't expect to catch it. I thought it would fall somewhere nearby, but by the grace of God I managed to catch it." According to Mehran, immediately after the catch the Swat Premier League organisers announced a prize of 10,000 Pakistani rupees (about £27.60) for him, funded by the Pakistan Army. The Marghazar resident was caught by surprise when the recording of the catch spread so quickly online, saying: "The video went viral overnight. I didn't even know about it." He expressed his happiness at receiving the award, saying he was grateful to God, and added that he had returned the ball after taking the catch. "People are saying I was taking the ball away with me, but that's not true. I returned it," he said. Swat Strikers won the match against GKR Dir by 34 runs, and Mehran urged the organisers to continue holding the tournament every year, describing it as an "excellent competition". Mehran Khan is from Marghazar in the Swat region of northern Pakistan [BBC] One of the most unusual catches There have been several remarkable catches by spectators at cricket matches in the past. In 1987, during a match in Australia, a cameraman casually caught one of former England all-rounder Ian Botham's sixes while holding a cigarette in his mouth. In 2014, during a New Zealand domestic match, a spectator slid down a slope and completed a one-handed catch. Last year, in a match between Australia and South Africa, a fan caught a ball with one hand while holding two drink cans in the other. Mehran's one-handed catch while sitting on a moving motorcycle will join them in cricketing history. Get cricket news sent straight to your phone

item.title: Trev Alberts' attorney plans to file lawsuit against Michigan
item.description: Lawyers for Trev Alberts, who had been hired by Michigan as its next athletic director before the university’s President-elect C. Cybele Raver and current Michigan President Domenico Grasso formally withdrew the university's offer of employment this week, are planning to file a lawsuit against the University of Michigan seeking millions in damages. Alberts’ attorney, Tom Mars, told The Detroit News on Wednesday, Nov. 25, the lawsuit could be filed in a “few weeks” either in Texas, where Alberts had been athletic director at Texas A&M before Michigan hired him, or in Michigan. Raver, who does not begin her tenure at Michigan until Dec. 1, hired Alberts and may also be included as a defendant in the case, Mars said. “It's just a straight up breach of contract,” said Mars, noted for high-profile college sports litigation, including coaching and administrative disputes. “They agreed to pay him $17.2 million plus $4 million, and then they changed their mind after they induced him to leave his job.” Mars said the memorandum of understanding is contractually binding and Michigan will have to pay the full contract, $17,205,352. The MOU had no reference to a background check that would prevent Alberts from being hired. Michigan also had agreed to pay Alberts’ $4 million buyout to Texas A&M. Alberts is now responsible to pay the buyout. “I want to put the whole case together and show Michigan what it looks like,” Mars said, “and then they can decide whether they want to spend the time and the energy defending it or not.” Alberts was hired by Michigan on Nov. 17 and signed a memorandum of understanding. He had not been formally announced as Michigan’s next athletic director replacing Warde Manuel, who planned to step down at the end of this year . Alberts was informed late Monday night, Nov. 23, he would no longer be the Michigan athletic director by a representative from the search firm ZRG Turnkey, which Michigan hired for its national search. Manuel, on Wednesday, agreed to remain at Michigan until an interim or permanent athletic director is hired. Michigan cited the results of a background check in its decision to rescind Alberts' hiring , saying the information gathered during the employment process provided "good cause" to end its agreement with him, according to a letter dated Tuesday, Nov. 24 sent to Alberts. The letter, signed by Grasso and Raver, formally withdrew the university's offer of employment and ended negotiations with Alberts "with good cause to terminate the MOU." The change of heart from Michigan comes amid scrutiny of Alberts' comments in an ongoing federal lawsuit, first reported by The Detroit News, that accuses University of Nebraska-Lincoln officials, including Alberts, of mishandling a sexual relationship between an associate women's basketball coach and a player during his tenure as the athletic director. item.title: Caleb Williams Wants to Give Someone Else the Thanksgiving He Remembers
item.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Before Caleb Williams became the Chicago Bears’ quarterback, Thanksgiving football meant a spot on the couch beside his dad. His mom made creamed spinach, they grabbed a bag of Tostitos, and the games became part of the holiday. It’s a familiar scene for football fans: food on the table, family in the room and the television on while the afternoon slips into evening. Williams remembers watching the Dallas Cowboys and another NFC team playing while he and his dad enjoyed the snack. On Thursday, he’ll be on the other side of the screen. Williams and the Bears visit the Detroit Lions in a Thanksgiving game with far more at stake than holiday bragging rights. Both teams enter 8-2, and the winner will leave Ford Field alone atop the NFC North. For Williams, the occasion is also a chance to give another family a memory like the ones he grew up with. “Now I get to be a part of making memories for somebody else,” he said during his Tuesday press conference . “We want to go out there and we want to put on a show and have fun doing it.” A familiar tradition, a bigger stage Nov 28, 2013; Detroit, MI, USA; Fox reporter Erin Andrews interviews Detroit Lions quarterback Matthew Stafford (9) after the game against the Green Bay Packers during a NFL football game on Thanksgiving at Ford Field. Detroit won 40-10. Mandatory Credit: Tim Fuller-USA TODAY Sports The Lions have been a fixture of Thanksgiving football for generations. For Williams, playing in the game he once watched at home is part of what makes the opportunity special. “As a kid, you were sitting at home watching this with your parents,” he added. “I was sitting at home watching these games with my pops, eating some food that my mom made.” Now, children who settle in with their own families could spend the afternoon watching Williams try to deliver a statement win. The quarterback knows the matchup brings plenty of excitement, and he said games like this are easier to get up for. Chicago has won five straight, while Detroit brings a six-game winning streak into Thursday. Both teams have the same record, but the Bears are still looking for their first NFC North victory after earlier losses to Minnesota and Green Bay. The last Bears-Lions Thanksgiving meeting also gives this trip a complicated place in Chicago’s recent history. In 2024, Williams and the Bears rallied from a 23-7 deficit, only for the game to end after a mismanaged final sequence left a timeout unused. Head coach Matt Eberflus was fired the following day. Two years later, Williams returns with a different head coach and a team playing for first place. Ben Johnson, who was Detroit’s offensive coordinator for that 2024 game, now leads Chicago into a matchup against his former team. item.title: Set point #14: A season in review
item.description: There’s no denying the fact that there was a lot of bad this season. Northwestern finished the year 8-20 overall and 1-16 in the Big Ten, losing 14 straight games before beating Iowa in the final week. The ‘Cats were swept 10 times during Big Ten play and ranked at the bottom of the conference in most of the major statistical categories, including wins. The season started off with a disappointing loss to a George Mason team that went .500 in its conference slate, and ended with a stretch of 16 losses in 17 games. There’s no other way to put it: the ‘Cats were not a good volleyball team. However, as I’ve spent the majority of the past 13 editions of this column critiquing the lack of competitiveness shown by Northwestern, I’ll try to keep the season finale one of hope. And, don’t get it twisted, there is hope to be had. Maya Stillwell and Hayley Schaaf broke out as a freshman middle duo. Stillwell ended the year with 120 kills and a team-high 82 blocks while hitting .279 in her 100 sets played. Schaaf totaled 86 kills and 35 blocks while hitting a team-high .299. The two steadily improved throughout the year, and Stillwell looked like one of the conference’s better middle blockers at times toward the end of the season. Both Stillwell and Schaaf can improve their blocking rhythm and attacking precision heading into next season, but if both stay with the ‘Cats, they should form a youthful and exciting middle group when combined with sophomore Kayla Kauffman. Setter Ellie Stiernagle was another impressive freshman. Though she had some defensive issues at points throughout the season, she became the staple of Northwestern. Stiernagle started 26 of the 26 matches she appeared in, finishing the year with 910 assists. She also had 16 aces and 46 blocks to go along with 188 digs. At 6-foot-2, Stiernagle is tall enough to play all around, and she proved it throughout the year. Northwestern’s serve receive was a big problem this season, but Stiernagle frequently gave her hitters chances to swing despite less-than-ideal passes. Sophomore libero Lauren Dignan was the major bright spot on the defensive end. She averaged 3.59 digs per set, good for seventh in the Big Ten, totaling 337. Although it was hard to defend with a questionable NU block often allowing clean hits or weird touches, Dignan did the best she could to cover the entire floor. Northwestern had three quality liberos on the roster, including Drew Wright and Gigi Navarrete, but Dignan was the one most trusted in the opposite-colored jersey. If the block can improve and the passing around her is shored up, Dignan could be in for a breakout junior season. The other key pieces of the team that will return next season are the two kill leaders, junior opposite hitter Mara Stiglic and sophomore outside hitter Bella Bullington. item.title: Mike McCarthy addresses Aaron Rodgers’ explosive criticism, confirms ’embarrassing’ Packers gaffe
item.description: Credit: Pittsburgh Steelers On Wednesday, now-former Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers unloaded on coach Mike McCarthy after his demotion from the starting lineup. Afterward, McCarthy had a chance to respond. Late Tuesday night, the Steelers announced in a statement that Rodgers had been benched in favor of backup Mason Rudolph. Given the odd hour and the lack of explanation for the sudden change, speculation ran wild over what led to the decision. Rodgers got the chance to offer his side of the story on Wednesday with a visit to his old stomping grounds , The Pat McAfee Show . There, the four-time NFL MVP went off, accusing McCarthy of repeatedly falling asleep during team meetings, failing to make an effort to get to know the defensive players, and broadly suggesting the Steelers’ head coach is struggling to keep up with the rigors of coaching an NFL team. Rodgers also spilled some embarrassing details about McCarthy, including “snoring” during meetings and ending a halftime speech against the Eagles by saying “one, two, three, Packers.” The Steelers released Rodgers following the appearance. Later on Wednesday, McCarthy met with the media as Pittsburgh prepares to play the Broncos on Friday. Embarrassing moment, but I just think we work a lot of hours, so definitely a difference of opinion from what I was told about the comments. “Aaron and I have a long history. He has a lot of opinions, and those are things we always talked about. item.title: Steelers Legend Backs Aaron Rodgers’ Claims About Mike McCarthy
item.description: Pittsburgh Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy talks before practice on Sept. 23, 2026. -- Ed Thompson / Steelers Now Pittsburgh Steelers great James Harrison is known to voice his honest opinion about the team, good and bad. He confirmed Aaron Rodgers ’ accusations about Mike McCarthy are not coming out of nowhere during Wednesday’s thunderstorm of rumors. “This is not the first time I have heard of the kind of things Aaron Rodgers is talking about on the Pat McAfee Show,” Harrison shared on X. The Steelers media calamity began Tuesday night with the announcement Rodgers would be inactive for Friday’s game against the Denver Broncos. The fire burned more fiercely when Rodgers took to The Pat McAfee Show to share his end of the story. item.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Trey Lyles doesn’t need to score 20 points to leave a mark on a game. On Monday, nine points were enough for his impact to stand out in the box score if you looked all the way to the last column. The Minnesota Timberwolves outscored the Brooklyn Nets by 29 points during Lyles’ 24 minutes in their 142-116 victory. It was another productive night for a reserve who has become one of the most reliable pieces of Chris Finch’s rotation. That performance also helped sustain one of the more surprising numbers on Minnesota’s roster. Through 18 games, Lyles leads the Timberwolves’ regular rotation players with a plus-13.7 net rating , according to NBA.com . In other words, Minnesota has outscored opponents by 13.7 points per 100 possessions with him on the floor. There are two names above him on the full team list. Among the players Finch has regularly relied on, Lyles sits just ahead of Jaden McDaniels at plus-13.4 and LaMelo Ball at plus-13.3. A net rating doesn’t capture an individual player’s value on its own. It reflects what happens with all five players on the floor and can be influenced by lineups, opponents and a relatively small early-season sample. Still, for a veteran whose contributions don’t always command attention, the number offers a reason to look more closely. item.title: The Galaxy keep missing the playoffs. Fans want ownership to take action
item.description: Galaxy forward Kyogo Furuhashi reacts during a match against Seattle at Dignity Health Sports Park on Sept. 12. After winning the MLS Cup title in 2024, the Galaxy haven't returned to the playoffs. (Luiza Moraes / Getty Images) Statistically, it’s far easier to make the MLS playoffs than it is to miss them. Eighteen of 30 teams qualify for the postseason, meaning each one starts the season with a 60% chance of making the playoffs. No other major professional sports league in the U.S. is as generous. Yet the Galaxy failed to make the cut this year. And last year. In fact, the Galaxy have missed the playoffs four times in six years since Greg Vanney took over as manager. They also missed in three of the four seasons before Vanney arrived, meaning the Galaxy have cleared the lowest playoff bar in American sports just three times in the last decade. And they haven’t done it in consecutive seasons since Bruce Arena was the coach. Read more: Mauricio Pochettino's exit places U.S. men's soccer in a precarious state Arena left a decade ago. (To be fair, the last time the Galaxy did reach the playoffs, in 2024, Vanney guided them to a championship .) But wait, there’s more. Home attendance was down, dropping below the 20,000 per-game average for the first time in a non-COVID season since the Galaxy left the Rose Bowl for Carson in 2003. That’s a decrease of more than 18% since 2023. All this should be concerning for the team and its owners at AEG. The Galaxy, after all, used to be the model MLS franchise. It won the most games, had the best players, collected the most titles and led the league in attendance nine times. Today? Not so much. So does AEG have a plan to fix that? We reached out to Dan Beckerman , AEG’s president and chief executive, through a company spokesman, hoping for some clues. We never heard back. However, general manager Will Kuntz , speaking in a videoconference with the media Friday, agreed things are dismal. “I don’t think we did a good enough job collectively last year,” he said. “So for us, it’s really about taking a hard look at everything we’ve done process-wise and saying ‘hey, how can we be better?’ Because it cannot continue like this.” Galaxy coach Greg Vanney reacts during a match against LAFC at BMO Stadium on Oct. 25. (Luke Hales / Getty Images) Yet Kuntz, the architect of the MLS Cup team, may not be around to see that process through. Vanney still has two years left on his lucrative contract while Kuntz’s deal ends next month, so if there’s going to be a fall guy for the Galaxy’s recent failures, it’s likely to be the GM, not the coach. On Friday, Kuntz was already speaking of the team in the past tense. “I really enjoyed my time at the Galaxy. I love being here,” he said. “I’d like to be back if it was up to me. But it’s not.” Nor is it up to the team’s most loyal supporters, who would like to see someone sacrificed for the team’s fall from grace. item.title: Cavan Sullivan named MLS Young Player of the Year 🌟
item.description: Cavan Sullivan named MLS Young Player of the Year 🌟 Philadelphia Union and USMNT midfielder Cavan Sullivan has capped a record-setting regular season by being named the 2026 MLS Young Player of the Year. In his first full campaign, the Man City-bound starlet emerged as one of the league's most exciting young talents, finishing with with a career-high 23 goal contributions (nine goals, 14 assists) in 29 appearances, and recorded a goal contribution in 10 consecutive matches, the longest such run by a teenager in MLS history. Both his total of 23 goal contributions and his 14 assists are the most ever by a teenager in a single MLS season. Sullivan's form also earned him MLS Player of the Month honors for September 2026. At 17 years and two days old, he became the youngest winner of the award in league history. His production on the club level soon translated to the international stage. Sullivan received his first call-up to the US men's national team in September and made his debut against Peru, becoming the second-youngest player in USMNT history to start a match. He has since collected four senior caps and added another milestone to his résumé by scoring against Mexico at 17 years and five days old, making him the youngest goalscorer in USMNT history.

item.title: How Columbus Crew turned it all around to set up MLS playoff showdown vs. Messi
item.description: It wasn’t working. Issa Tall had to admit that. Well, he didn’t really have to. The results told the story for him. The Columbus Crew didn’t win in its first five MLS matches. By the World Cup break, 15 games in, they’d only added two more. There needed to be changes, and they needed to be big. The Crew general manager moved quickly. In May, he fired coach Henrik Rydström, his first coaching hire as the Crew’s chief soccer officer, though he was quick to point out he was involved with previous hires including bringing in Wilfried Nancy. He spent big in the summer, revamping the Crew’s attack and adding pieces while bidding farewell to some regulars. Ten players arrived, and eight went out. It worked. The Crew turned the boat around, going from worst in the Eastern Conference to closing the season on a six-game win streak and having won eight of their last nine. That was enough not only to jump out of Thursday’s wild card match but to set up a First Round playoff series with Inter Miami, the reigning champion led by Lionel Messi. They also pushed to the U.S. Open Cup final, falling to St. Louis City in a penalty shootout. All of it led Tall to believe he made the right decisions, moving on quickly from the coach he thought was the right man for the job. “Some people could’ve waited the full year. Maybe it would’ve been safer, but that’s not me. That’s not us as a club. That’s not even the way we play!” Tall told USA TODAY Sports ahead of the playoffs. “You see how we are bold and are not afraid of taking risk. At the end of the day, it wasn’t even a risk necessarily. It was necessary for our players, for our club as a whole and I think ultimately we made the right decision to do it at that time.” Tall still stands by Rydström as a good coach, something he’s proving while leading Hammarby in Sweden which currently sits atop of the table after running off five consecutive wins. But he wasn’t the right fit for the Crew in the post-Nancy era. The Crew turned to Courtois, a former Crew academy and MLS Next Pro coach who continued the idea first expressed on the field so successfully by Nancy’s teams. The squad might not have been the entirely right squad, either. Tall turned to a scouting network led by Mark Nichols, bringing in a proven MLS veteran in Santi Rodriguez, Chile national team forward Gonzalo Tapia, securing a loan deal for Moroccan winger Anass Zaroury and signing designated player Brais Mendez, a Spanish attacker whose arrival from Real Sociedad brought to mind that of Cucho Hernandez. item.title: Gotham FC’s title defense comes to crushing end in semifinal loss after venue change
item.description: They came by car, by the special-event X80 bus, by bike if they were feeling sporty. They came in layers, in beanies and scarves, with Gotham’s black-and-sky-blue colors on top. They came on behalf of those who couldn’t come, capacity being reduced at this impromptu change of venue, each one trying to make noise for five. Gotham FC forward Sam Kerr (20) competes for the ball against Kansas City Current defender Gabrielle Robinson (24) on Sunday, Nov. 15, 2026, in New York City. IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect They came with some measure of outrage — these home-field shenanigans would never happen in men’s sports — while their better angels told them to come in joy, in celebration, everyone watching women’s sports. And then, 25 miles and 20,000 seats removed from their regular destination at New Jersey’s Sports Illustrated Stadium, huddled in the bleachers by a blue track ringing an immaculate pitch at Icahn Stadium on Randall’s Island, in the shadow of the old Psychiatric Center and with the light fading over the Costco across the river, 5,000 devoted souls Sunday afternoon watched Gotham’s NWSL title defense end in a 2-1 semifinal loss to the Kansas City Current. “We lost today because we weren’t the better team,” Gotham winger and oracle Midge Purce said. “That being said, I would say it’s inexcusable. It’s not what you want in a professional league. It’s not what you want for women who are progressing in the United States and supposed to be one of the best leagues in the entire world. I think it’s a bad look for everyone involved. And we always want to be at Sports Illustrated in front of our fans when we earned that right throughout the season. But I would say it had no effect on performance today.” The match had been moved to Icahn on Monday due to concerns over the disintegrating field conditions at Sports Illustrated, which had unfortunately overshadowed Gotham’s quarterfinal victory there last weekend. Gotham was unbeaten in its past 13 matches at Sports Illustrated, which is operated by the Red Bulls of MLS. Croix Bethune, left, celebrates scoring a goal with Kansas City Current teammate Lo’eau LaBonta during an NWSL playoff match in New York, Nov. 15, 2026. Getty Images “I think that’s also part of the sadness,” head coach Juan Carlos Amorós said. “I think we never know what would have happened if we played on a good pitch. I think it was the right decision to come here. I think the pitch in the other stadium was unfortunately unplayable.” Tickets for the semifinal were reallotted and grabbed up in a hurry, while Gotham officials ground on the logistics of moving their game-day operations. “Obviously not ideal we had to change stadiums, but … I think that’s really awesome to come into a new environment, a new stadium, you have to adapt, you have to make sure you can bring that energy and our supporters did that tonight and that’s incredible,” Gotham midfielder Savannah McCaskill said. item.title: Beckham to be inducted into US Soccer Hall of Fame
item.description: David Beckham was knighted by King Charles in 2025 [Getty Images] David Beckham will be inducted into the United States' National Soccer Hall of Fame as part of its 2027 class. The former Manchester United and England midfielder, 51, made headlines in 2007 when he moved to Los Angeles from Spanish giants Real Madrid to join Major League Soccer (MLS) side LA Galaxy on a five-year contract. He made 124 appearances in all competitions for Galaxy, scoring 20 goals, and twice won both the MLS Cup and Supporters' Shield. Beckham's six seasons at Galaxy helped to raise the global profile of MLS and following his retirement in 2013, he became co-owner of MLS club Inter Miami, who signed Argentina World Cup winner Lionel Messi in 2023. His induction ceremony is set to take place on 16 April 2027 in Frisco, Texas. David Beckham's deal with LA Galaxy in 2007 was reportedly worth £128m [Getty Images] He was told the news he had been chosen on the veterans' ballot at an MLS board of governors' meeting on Thursday and said his time in the US has been "an incredible journey". Beckham, who had two loan spells with AC Milan in 2009 and 2010 while at Galaxy, added: "I'm looking to build this league and this sport in this great country for a long time." Meanwhile, former US internationals Megan Rapinoe and Julie Ertz have also been voted into the Hall of Fame in their first year of eligibility. Ballon d'Or winner Rapinoe, 41, and midfielder Ertz, 34, lifted the Women’s World Cup twice with with the US in 2015 and 2019. "To be alongside all the greatest players that have played for us, and played for our country alongside a bunch of my team-mates and friends, recognised like that in this way just means you were successful and a part of great teams," Rapinoe wrote on Instagram. item.title: Gotham FC’s home semifinal moved to 5K-seat stadium in field quality debacle
item.description: Seattle Reign FC defender Phoebe McClernon, left, defends Gotham FC forward Guro Reiten during an NWSL playoff game in Harrison, N.J., Sunday, Nov. 8, 2026. For the first time in franchise history, Gotham FC is set to host its semifinal match next weekend. But there’s an unfortunate twist. Gotham’s semifinal match against the Kansas City Current won’t be played at the club’s typical stomping grounds in Harrison, New Jersey. Instead, Gotham agreed to move Sunday’s match to Icahn Stadium on Randall’s Island for better playing surface quality. “This was an extremely difficult decision, and one we did not take lightly,” Gotham president of soccer operations Yael Averbuch West said in a letter to fans. “After thoughtful consultation with coach Juan Carlos Amorós, our team captains, and our ownership, we felt it was important to prioritize a playing surface that appropriately allows our athletes to perform at their best. Providing our players with a high-quality surface to compete is a responsibility we take very seriously.” The Gotham FC starting eleven line up before the NWSL playoff quarterfinal in Harrison, N.J., Sunday, Nov. 8, 2026. Lev Radin/Shutterstock Gotham is a tenant of Major League Soccer’s Red Bull New York at Sports Illustrated Stadium. The Red Bulls are scheduled to play an exhibition game there Saturday night, exacerbating concerns about the field quality. The state of Sports Illustrated Stadium’s pitch has been a cause for concern over the past two weeks. ESPN reported the NWSL fined Gotham $10,000 for poor field conditions during last week’s regular-season finale, after which the club was awarded its first league Shield. The pitch condition was once again a major sticking point after Gotham’s ugly quarterfinal win against the Seattle Reign. Retiring Reign midfielder Jess Fishlock called the field “atrocious.” Gotham defender Jess Carter was overheard saying the grounds were “so bad” when walking through the tunnel after the match. A week after Jaelin Howell injured her right ankle during a home game, the Gotham midfielder said the field was “pretty sandy” and “a little unstable.” Amorós acknowledged the rough conditions impacted the quality of the game. Seattle Reign FC defender Phoebe McClernon, left, defends Gotham FC forward Guro Reiten during an NWSL playoff game in Harrison, N.J., Sunday, Nov. 8, 2026. item.title: NYCFC fires head coach Pascal Jansen after second-half collapse
item.description: NYCFC has fired head coach Pascal Jansen. New York City FC will be looking for a new head coach this offseason. Less than 24 hours after the club played its final match of the 2026 season, NYCFC announced that it fired head coach Pascal Jansen following a disappointing campaign that saw the club miss the playoffs for only the third time in its 12-year history. NYCFC went through an ugly 2026 season, finishing 11th in the Eastern Conference and being knocked out of playoff contention before the club even reached its Decision Day matchup with D.C. United on Saturday. The rough season was highlighted by the massive second-half collapse NYCFC went through following the World Cup break, posting a 5W-8D-6L record and sliding from eighth place to 11th. Jansen was informed of the decision by the club’s front office on Sunday morning and ultimately the decision to move on from him as head coach came down to the “failure of making playoffs” following a “disappointing season,” a source told The Post. NYCFC has fired head coach Pascal Jansen. Getty Images The head coaching role will take on an even bigger role going into 2027 as NYCFC prepares for massive changes with the planned move into their new stadium and MLS changing their league calendar to a summer-through-spring format, which is in line with the European football calendar and includes an abbreviated sprint season that will run from February to May. The club views this next year as a “crucial point in franchise history” and the feeling is that NYCFC wants to make sure it has “the right leadership in place,” the source added. NYCFC will begin its search for a new head coach immediately, sporting director Todd Dunivant said in a statement released late Sunday morning. “We would like to thank Pascal for his commitment and contributions to New York City FC and wish him and his family all the best. This decision follows a thorough review of the season and reflects our ambition as an organization,” he said. item.title: Messi makes history with MLS Golden Boot
item.description: Messi retired from international football with Argentina earlier this year [Getty Images] Inter Miami forward Lionel Messi has become the first player in MLS history to win the Golden Boot in consecutive seasons. The eight-time Ballon d'Or winner scored 26 goals in 31 appearances, four clear of FC Dallas striker Peter Musa and five more than Nashville's English forward Sam Surridge. Messi becomes only the sixth player to land the award twice, joining a list that includes former Charlton Athletic and Southampton striker Bradley Wright-Phillips. In addition to his goals, the 39-year-old notched 17 assists over the course of the MLS season, ensuring his 43 goal contributions was also a league best for the second year in a row. And the World Cup winner could soon make more history as he bids to become the first three-time Landon Donovan MLS MVP winner. The former Argentina forward landed the award in 2024 as Inter Miami won the Supporters' Shield title and also in 2025 as they won the MLS Cup. Despite Messi's magic, Miami weren't able to land top spot in the MLS Eastern Conference, with the team finishing 17 points behind Surridge's Nashville. They will now face Columbus Crew over three games in the first round of the MLS Cup play-offs which begin later this month.
